title: Causal-break non-Markovian channel identification
difficulty_explanation: System-only causal breaks do not erase the retained memory. From system Pauli readouts alone, the inverse must distinguish a complex exchange phase, coherent ZZ and memory phases, and finite-temperature damping, then predict unseen intervention sequences.
solution_explanation: The expert builds the retained system-memory evolution with TensorCircuit DMCircuit custom collision gates, reset channels, and generalized amplitude-damping channels, then performs deterministic bounded multi-start nonlinear least squares.
verification_explanation: A TensorCircuit-free NumPy density-matrix oracle independently composes unitary conjugations and Kraus maps, hides seeded parameter instances, and checks both parameter recovery and unseen causal-break trajectories.
conditioning_notes: The exchange-phase interval is narrower than one period and all hidden parameters are interior. Known phase-referenced memory preparations and diverse X/Y system controls and readouts remove the exchange-phase gauge. Only system observables are exposed; causal breaks make retained-memory effects identifiable rather than reducible to one fitted system channel.
api_risks: Requires TensorCircuit-NG DMCircuit.unitary, DMCircuit.reset, DMCircuit.amplitudedamping(gamma, p), and append-after-densitymatrix(reuse=False) behavior in the pinned image. The expert requests complex128 and uses finite-difference steps larger than contraction noise.
